The test includes fractional seconds and a null value.|
**Change:** Bug fix · **Severity of issue fixed:** Medium
Merge Risk: Minimal · up to c5291

Snowflake TIME columns are now kept as ISO text instead of being turned into missing values, and time-only strings are no longer inferred as timestamps. Regression tests cover the changed behavior, and no merge-blocking risk is identified.
Security architecture risk: Low · up to c5291

TIME columns intentionally become text, and time-only samples no longer infer as timestamps. These changes can affect consumers of column metadata, but the reviewed paths do not introduce new data-access or execution authority. **Retained concerns** No architecture-level concerns identified.
Security review details

**Security Blast Radius** - _inferred_ — The demonstrated exposure is data-dependent representation and metadata classification within already retrieved samples. Because timestamp inference is shared, its changed classification is not limited to Snowflake, but no reviewed path turns that classification into additional access authority. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Retrieval continues to use the existing Snowflake connection and query paths. The changed logic operates after fetch and does not add a connection, credential source, query-execution capability, or authorization decision. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — On the traced Snowflake sample path, conversion operates on a freshly materialized frame before cache publication, containing partial-conversion failures locally. Repetition skips the new branch once the column becomes Arrow string. Sanitization remains sequential and in-place, so this does not establish whole-frame atomicity for arbitrary external callers supplying shared frames.

Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title names the main change: Snowflake TIME values are kept as ISO text instead of being converted to NaT. It matches the changeset (SnowTable dtype mapping, Table._sanitize ISO conversion, and contains_timestamp change) and the linked objectives. It uses the conventional fix(rfm) prefix and is 63 characters long.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description states the bug, the cause (TIME mapped to Dtype.time, then coerced to NaT by to_datetime), and the fix (Dtype.string plus ISO text conversion and a contains_timestamp change). It also lists the tests, the verification results, and the scope limit to Snowflake. It is directly related to the changeset.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** Issue `#88` (direct, open) requires that Snowflake TIME values not be dropped as missing. It accepts text as a model-compatible form. The PR maps Snowflake TIME to Dtype.string in SnowTable._to_dtype, so the column no longer goes through to_datetime. Table._sanitize converts Arrow time-of-day columns to ISO text (HH:MM:SS, with fractional seconds at the column's unit) and keeps nulls null. contains_timestamp no longer infers a timestamp for columns made only of times of day. The test test_time_columns_are_kept_as_text_not_dropped covers second, millisecond, microsecond and nanosecond precision, and checks dtype, stype, absence of warnings and sampled values. The PR reports that these tests fail on main and pass with the change. The raw summary is consistent with this. Verification relies on the PR description and summary, not on a repository read of the final code.
Full details: Out of Scope Changes check

**Explanation** All changes connect to issue `#88`. The changes are: the TIME dtype mapping in snow/table.py; the time-of-day conversion in rfm/base/table.py; the time-of-day exclusion in metadata_inference/timestamp.py; the Snowflake regression tests; the timestamp inference test; and the CHANGELOG entry. The timestamp inference change supports the requirement that a time-of-day text column is not inferred as a timestamp. The CHANGELOG entry is documentation for the fix. DuckDB and Postgres mappings are unchanged, as the PR states. This matches the Snowflake scope of `#88`. No unrelated change is evident from the summary.
